page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Storage is network-attached with a capacity of 1 GB, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core performance metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 25%. Database operations on PassMark are particularly limited, registering in the bottom 10% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers dedicated CPU resources and strong single-threaded execution capabilities at an entry-level resource scale, though it is constrained by network-attached storage and low multi-core scaling. It is suitable for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded CPU performance, such as basic text processing, lightweight static web serving, or simple single-threaded utility scripts. It is less suitable for multi-threaded compilation, database hosting, or memory-intensive operations due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks.
